spatial_claims.claim: Cone K and cylinder C share the same circular base (center E) and the same height h. Cone apex is directly above E at height h.
Square inscribed in the base circle; square is greater than half the circle. Successive arc bisections produce inscribed polygons where each new triangle exceeds half its circular segment.
Inscribed polygon Q in the circle yields prism Pr(Q) inside cylinder C, with C - Pr(Q) < S.
Polygon Q is divided into triangles from center E; E is interior to Q. Each triangular prism has height h equal to the cylinder height.

Each triangular prism decomposes into three equal pyramids by 12.7. The pyramid on each triangle with apex at cone vertex (E,h) has height h, so Prism(T,h) = 3 * Pyramid(T,h). Summing: Pr(Q) = 3 * Pyr(Q).
Pyr(Q) is contained within cone K because Q is inscribed in the base circle and the pyramid shares the cone's apex. Hence Pyr(Q) < K.
Circumscribed polygon Q' about the base circle. Excess of Q' over circle, times height, is less than S.

Cylinder C is contained within prism Pr(Q') since Q' contains the base circle. Cone K is contained within pyramid Pyr(Q') since Q' contains the base circle and they share the same apex. Hence Pyr(Q') > K.

Pr(Q') = 3 * Pyr(Q') by 12.7 applied to constituent triangles of Q' (formed from center E). E is interior to Q'. Each triangular prism decomposes into three equal pyramids, pyramid height equals prism height h.

configuration_map: The configuration consists of a cone K and cylinder C sharing a circular base (center E) and height h. The cone apex is at point (E, h) directly above center E. In Case 1, an inscribed polygon Q lies inside the circle, so the prism Pr(Q) lies inside C and the pyramid Pyr(Q) (apex at cone vertex) lies inside K. In Case 2, a circumscribed polygon Q' contains the circle, so C lies inside Pr(Q') and K lies inside Pyr(Q'). In both cases, Q (or Q') is decomposed into triangles from center E, which is interior to both Q and Q'. Each triangular prism of height h decomposes by 12.7 into three pyramids, and the pyramid with the same triangular base and apex at (E, h) has the same height h as the prism. All containment relations are mutually consistent throughout the proof.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are straightforward containment relations (inscribed/circumscribed polygons, prisms inside/outside cylinders, pyramids inside/outside cones) that are mutually consistent. The 12.7 volume decomposition (prism = 3 * pyramid) is correctly applied in both the inscribed and circumscribed cases, with the pyramid height matching the prism height in each case. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior point ambiguities, and no ray-ordering claims are present. The proof uses a standard double exhaustion argument with no spatial configuration contradictions.
